boundary: Pass 6152 proves a theorem about characteristic 3 and closes the gap Pass 6138 located. It does NOT supply a distinguisher -- it proves none can exist internally. Pass 6154 re-tests the one surviving batch claim and finds it generic; that does not make it wrong

pass_6152_no_cube_root_in_characteristic.proof_1: F_Q has an element of order 3 iff 3 divides Q-1; and 3^k - 1 = 2 mod 3 always
pass_6152_no_cube_root_in_characteristic.proof_2: x^3 - 1 = (x-1)^3 in characteristic 3, so 1 is a TRIPLE root and the only cube root of unity
pass_6152_no_cube_root_in_characteristic.so: F_9 does not contain omega, F_27 does not, F_3^k does not for any k
pass_6152_no_cube_root_in_characteristic.theorem: no field of characteristic 3 contains a primitive cube root of unity

pass_6153_the_arc_closes_as_a_theorem.now_settled: the distinguisher requires canonically choosing a primitive cube root of unity, because the character field is Q(omega). Characteristic 3 PROVABLY CANNOT SUPPLY ONE, at any extension degree
pass_6153_the_arc_closes_as_a_theorem.the_statement: the substrate canonically POSES a binary chirality question (Pass 6104: perfect group, non-self-dual Weil constituents, unswappable pair) and PROVABLY CANNOT ANSWER IT internally (here). Both halves are theorems
pass_6153_the_arc_closes_as_a_theorem.what_was_open: Pass 6138 found no substrate-internal distinguisher between U and U*, and left open whether one might exist in an extension -- F_9 was the obvious candidate since W(3,3) has F_9 subquadrangle structure
pass_6153_the_arc_closes_as_a_theorem.why_that_is_better_than_a_gap: an unfilled gap invites more searching. A proof of impossibility says the answer must come from outside the substrate, which is a structural statement about where the input has to enter

pass_6154_the_surviving_batch_claim_is_g.claim: BT1644 -- W(3,3)'s collinearity graph is Ramanujan and satisfies the Ihara RH
pass_6154_the_surviving_batch_claim_is_g.the_change_the_object_test: W(3,q) has eigenvalues k = q(q+1), r = q-1, s = -(q+1). Ramanujan needs |s| <= 2*sqrt(k-1), i.e. (q+1)^2 <= 4(q^2+q-1), i.e. 3q^2 + 2q - 5 >= 0, i.e. (3q+5)(q-1) >= 0 -- TRUE for every q >= 1
pass_6154_the_surviving_batch_claim_is_g.verdict: W(3,q) is Ramanujan for EVERY q, not just q=3. The property is generic across the family and says nothing about q=3 specifically
pass_6154_the_surviving_batch_claim_is_g.which_leaves: of the whole Aug 18 batch, the mathematics that survives is correct and generic; the parts that were specific to q=3 were the framing, and those did not survive
